title: Poland's Clean Air programme speeds phase-out of coal home heating
problem: Coal and other polluting fuels burned in household heating devices caused severe air pollution.
solution: The national Clean Air programme funds the replacement of outdated household heating devices.
funding: Public funding for replacing outdated heating devices; no amount is reported.
results: E3G reports significant progress in phasing out coal in individual heating installations. Poland's heat pump market also grew 120% in 2022 compared with 2021, helped by the energy crisis.
serbia_reason: Many Serbian households still heat with coal and wood in old stoves, so a national device-replacement scheme targets a similar problem.
adapt_needed: Link replacement grants to efficient clean devices such as heat pumps and to income, so energy-poor households can take part.
blockers: Low household incomes and cheap, poorly regulated coal and firewood.
quote: Efforts to combat air pollution have led to significant progress in phasing out coal and other polluting fuels in individual heating installations, supported by initiatives like the Clean Air program, which funds the replacement of outdated heating devices.

title: Poland modernises district heating but keeps coal in long-term plans
programme: Poland national heating and cooling strategy and NECP
problem: Poland runs some of the largest district heating networks in Central and Eastern Europe and must decarbonise them.
solution: The national strategy centres on modernising district heating networks and making them more efficient, alongside pilots in low-temperature heating (Szczecin), waste heat recovery (Poznan) and geothermal heat (Poddebice, Stargard).
implementer: Government of Poland and city district heating operators
results: The new NECP raises the renewable heating and cooling target from 21.4% to 32.1%, and pilots prove the business case. But neither the strategy nor the NECP sets specific measures to phase out fossil fuels, and coal stays in long-term district heating plans.
serbia_reason: Serbia also has large municipal heat networks, some still fed by coal and lignite. Poland shows that network modernisation without a coal exit date leaves heat locked into coal.
adapt_needed: Pair network modernisation with a dated coal exit plan for each heat plant and scale up proven pilots.
blockers: Cheap domestic lignite and the cost of replacing coal-fired heat capacity.
quote: The strategy does not explicitly outline specific measures and targets for decarbonising heating and phasing out fossil fuels, and nor does the NECP. Coal use is still envisaged in long-term plans for district heating plants.

title: Slovakia lifts renewable heating target to offset nuclear-heavy power mix
programme: Slovakia updated NECP – renewable heating and cooling target
problem: With nuclear at nearly 60% of power, Slovakia has little room to raise renewables in electricity, and its district heating depends heavily on fossil gas.
solution: The government raised the renewable target for heating and cooling in its updated NECP and is piloting geothermal heat sources.
results: The heating and cooling renewables target rose from 19% to 28%, making heating the main contributor to Slovakia's overall renewables target. Gas still dominates, and the European Commission urges biomethane, diversification and gas demand reduction.
serbia_reason: Serbian district heating is also heavily gas-based, and heat is an obvious place to raise the renewables share.
adapt_needed: Set a separate renewable heat target in the NECP with geothermal and heat pump measures behind it.
blockers: Gas-based heat plants with long remaining lifetimes and limited geothermal exploration data.
quote: To compensate to some extent the government have increased the RES ambition in heating and cooling from 19% to 28%.

title: Bulgaria's high renewable heating target relies heavily on household firewood
programme: Bulgaria updated NECP – renewable heating and cooling target
problem: Bulgaria must decarbonise heating, where firewood is widespread and Sofia District Heating consumes one-third of the country's gas imports.
solution: The updated NECP sets a 43.66% renewables target for heating and cooling by 2030.
results: Much of the target rests on firewood, which supplies 36% of heating in inhabited households. Heating is already electrified in 48% of inhabited homes, but often with inefficient devices.
serbia_reason: Serbia's renewable heat share also leans on household fuelwood, so a headline target can hide unsustainable burning.
adapt_needed: Count only sustainable biomass towards targets and plan to turn firewood into a back-up heat source.
blockers: Household dependence on cheap fuelwood and weak data on wood use.
quote: Yet much of this contribution comes from the burning of firewood in homes, which accounts for 36% of the heating in inhabited households.

title: EU efficiency directive requires heating plans in cities over 45,000
programme: Energy Efficiency Directive (EED) – municipal heating and cooling plans
problem: Many EU member states lack comprehensive heating strategies and local heat planning.
solution: The revised EED obliges municipalities above 45,000 people to prepare heating and cooling plans, requires heating and cooling assessments in NECPs and sets targets for renewables and waste heat in district heating by 2050.
implementer: European Commission and EU member states
results: Local plans must support the shift to renewable heat and away from fossil fuels, but the directive still allows fossil gas in efficient district heating until 2030, which E3G flags as a concern.
serbia_reason: As an EU candidate and Energy Community member, Serbia is expected to align with EU efficiency law, which would bring municipal heat planning to its larger cities. Starting these plans early would help Serbian heat utilities prepare bankable projects.
adapt_needed: Set a population threshold and a simple planning template that Serbian municipalities and their heat companies can use.
blockers: Limited planning capacity and data in municipalities and heat utilities.
quote: Municipalities with populations exceeding 45,000 are mandated to develop municipal heating and cooling plans, while member states are required to include heating and cooling assessments in their National Energy and Climate Plans (NECPs).

title: EU buildings directive ends fossil boiler subsidies, targets 2040 phase-out
problem: Fossil fuel boilers in buildings lock in emissions and gas dependence for decades.
solution: The revised EPBD aims to phase out fossil fuel boilers by 2040, ends subsidies for standalone fossil boilers after 2025, introduces one-stop-shops for renovation and phases in solar on buildings.
implementer: European Commission and EU member states
results: Solar requirements start with new public and commercial buildings by 2026 and reach existing public buildings by 2030. E3G warns that promoting 'hybrid heating systems' may open the door to hydrogen boilers.
serbia_reason: Serbia will need to align its building rules and household heating subsidies with EU law as it moves towards accession.
adapt_needed: Phase fossil boilers out of national and municipal heating subsidy schemes on a published timetable.
blockers: Wide reliance on gas and individual boilers and limited budgets for clean alternatives.
quote: While the directive aims to phase out fossil fuel boilers by 2040 and end subsidies for standalone boilers powered by fossil fuels after 2025, concerns persist over the promotion of “hybrid heating systems with a significant share of RES”, which may inadvertently pave the way for hydrogen boilers with concerns over their economic efficiency and safety.
